source_metadata.title: Effects of Dapagliflozin on 24-Hour Glycemic Control in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial
source_metadata.source_packet_note: The Drive source folder contained the nine publisher supplementary PDFs; the matching open-access primary article was resolved by DOI/PMID/PMCID for whole-source extraction.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study compared dapagliflozin with placebo for 24-hour glycemic profiles measured by continuous glucose monitoring in adults with inadequately controlled type 2 diabetes receiving stable metformin or insulin-based background therapy.
This was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, parallel-design study conducted at 34 United States centers between May and October 2015 (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02429258).

Participants were randomized 1:1 to dapagliflozin or placebo using an Interactive Voice Response System/Interactive Web Response System, with metformin versus insulin background therapy used as the randomization stratum.

The intention-to-treat and safety populations each included 100 randomized and treated participants: 50 assigned to dapagliflozin and 50 to placebo; the dapagliflozin arm included 23 metformin-stratum and 27 insulin-stratum participants, and placebo included 25 in each stratum.

Ninety-seven participants had adequate lead-in and week-4 CGM data and completed the study; two dapagliflozin participants withdrew consent and one placebo participant was withdrawn for a protocol violation.

population.label: Participants completing with adequate lead-in and week-4 CGM data

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible adults were 18–75 years old with type 2 diabetes treated for at least 8 weeks with stable metformin at least 1500 mg/day or insulin at least 30 units/day with or without up to two oral antidiabetes drugs.

population.label: Eligibility criteria
inclusion_criteria: Stable metformin ≥1500 mg/day or insulin ≥30 U/day ± up to two OADs for ≥8 weeks

atoms.canonical_statement: At screening, required measures included HbA1c 7.5%–10.5%, BMI at most 45 kg/m², fasting C-peptide at least 1.5 ng/mL, and at least 70% CGM compliance during lead-in.

Key exclusions included significant cardiovascular history, type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis within 12 months, bariatric surgery, bladder cancer, recent orthostatic hypotension, uncontrolled hypertension, at least two severe hypoglycemic episodes in the prior year, and recent medications affecting glucose metabolism or weight.

population.label: Key exclusion criteria
exclusion_criteria: Type 1 diabetes or DKA within 12 months
≥2 severe hypoglycemic episodes in prior 12 months
Recent medication affecting glucose metabolism or weight

atoms.canonical_statement: Participants assigned to dapagliflozin received dapagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily for 4 weeks in addition to their background metformin or insulin-based regimen.

exposures.details: Added to open-label metformin ≥1500 mg/day or insulin ≥30 U/day with or without up to two OADs.

atoms.canonical_statement: Participants assigned to control received matching placebo once daily for 4 weeks in addition to the same background-therapy framework.

exposures.details: Added to open-label metformin ≥1500 mg/day or insulin ≥30 U/day with or without up to two OADs.

atoms.canonical_statement: Dexcom G4 PLATINUM CGM measured interstitial glucose every 5 minutes (288 measurements/day) during a 7-day lead-in assessment and again during week 4; participants and investigators were blinded to CGM readings.
A standardized breakfast on days -13 and 22 contained 660 kcal (60% carbohydrate, 15% protein, 25% fat), with postprandial glucose blood sampling at 0, 30, 60, 120, 180, and 240 minutes.

Efficacy analyses used the ITT population; ANCOVA modeled change in 24-hour mean glucose with treatment and background-therapy stratum as factors and baseline value as a covariate, while linear mixed-effects models addressed missing data.

The study had 80% power to detect a 14.5 mg/dL difference in the primary outcome for the overall population; secondary and exploratory P values were nominal and the authors stated that treatment-difference inferences should not be made from them.
CGM profiles with fewer than 260 data points were censored; profiles with 260–287 points were considered valid and missing points were imputed by linear or cubic-spline interpolation.

In the insulin stratum (N=52), background regimens were long-acting insulin only in 2 (3.9%), long-acting insulin plus oral antidiabetes drugs in 13 (25.0%), rapid/short-acting plus long/intermediate-acting insulin only in 6 (11.5%), rapid/short-acting plus long/intermediate-acting insulin plus oral drugs in 17 (32.7%), and other regimens in 14 (26.9%).
The primary outcome was change from baseline to week 4 in 24-hour mean glucose derived from 7-day CGM data, calculated as 24-hour glucose AUC divided by 24 hours and expressed in mg/dL.

outcome.definition: AUC0–24 divided by 24 hours from CGM data

atoms.canonical_statement: CGM secondary ranges were defined as glucose below 70 mg/dL, 70–180 mg/dL, and above 180 mg/dL, summarized as percentage of monitored time.

concept.text: Percentage of CGM time in predefined glucose ranges

atoms.canonical_statement: Mean amplitude of glucose excursion (MAGE) was defined as the mean absolute nadir-to-peak difference for excursions exceeding the 24-hour CGM standard deviation.

outcome.definition: Mean absolute nadir-to-peak difference for excursions exceeding one 24-hour CGM SD

atoms.canonical_statement: The 24-hour “distance traveled” glucose-variability measure was the arc length of the glucose curve approximated with the trapezoid rule from a finite Fourier approximation of consecutive glucose measurements.

outcome.definition: Arc length of the 24-hour glucose curve using trapezoidal approximation of a finite Fourier representation

atoms.canonical_statement: At week 4, 24-hour mean glucose changed from 177.9 to 160.7 mg/dL with dapagliflozin and from 182.6 to 187.5 mg/dL with placebo; the least-squares mean treatment difference in change from baseline was -24.0 mg/dL (P<0.001).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: least-squares mean difference in change from baseline

atoms.canonical_statement: From baseline to week 4, mean time in the 70–180 mg/dL range increased by 12.2 percentage points with dapagliflozin (95% CI 7.0 to 17.3) and decreased by 2.8 points with placebo (95% CI -7.9 to 2.2).

outcome.definition: Percentage of CGM-monitored time in target range

quantitative_result.effect_measure: dapagliflozin mean change from baseline, percentage points

atoms.canonical_statement: From baseline to week 4, mean time with glucose >180 mg/dL decreased by 12.6 percentage points with dapagliflozin (95% CI -17.8 to -7.3) and increased by 3.5 points with placebo (95% CI -1.7 to 8.7).

outcome.definition: Percentage of CGM-monitored time above 180 mg/dL

quantitative_result.effect_measure: dapagliflozin mean change from baseline, percentage points

atoms.canonical_statement: From baseline to week 4, mean time with glucose <70 mg/dL increased by 0.3 percentage points with dapagliflozin (95% CI -0.3 to 0.9) and decreased by 0.6 points with placebo (95% CI -1.2 to -0.1).

outcome.definition: Percentage of CGM-monitored time below 70 mg/dL

quantitative_result.effect_measure: dapagliflozin mean change from baseline, percentage points

atoms.canonical_statement: Mean time with glucose <54 mg/dL was 0.0% at baseline and remained 0.0% at week 4 in both treatment groups.

outcome.definition: Percentage of CGM-monitored time below 54 mg/dL

quantitative_result.effect_measure: week-4 mean percentage of time in dapagliflozin arm

atoms.canonical_statement: In the metformin stratum, 24-hour mean glucose fell from 177.0 to 155.5 mg/dL with dapagliflozin and rose from 185.6 to 198.0 mg/dL with placebo; the LSM treatment difference was -36.2 mg/dL (nominal P<0.001).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: least-squares mean treatment difference in change from baseline

atoms.canonical_statement: In the insulin stratum, 24-hour mean glucose fell from 178.6 to 164.8 mg/dL with dapagliflozin and from 179.7 to 177.4 mg/dL with placebo; the LSM treatment difference was -11.9 mg/dL (nominal P=0.153).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: least-squares mean treatment difference in change from baseline

atoms.canonical_statement: For time in the 70–180 mg/dL target range, the reported treatment difference versus placebo was +23.8 percentage points in the metformin stratum (nominal P<0.001).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: treatment difference versus placebo in change from baseline, percentage points

atoms.canonical_statement: For time in the 70–180 mg/dL target range, the reported treatment difference versus placebo was +6.1 percentage points in the insulin stratum (nominal P=0.218).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: treatment difference versus placebo in change from baseline, percentage points

atoms.canonical_statement: The adjusted treatment difference in 2-hour postprandial glucose change from baseline was -36.3 mg/dL in the overall population (P<0.001).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: adjusted mean difference versus placebo in change from baseline

atoms.canonical_statement: The adjusted treatment difference in fasting plasma glucose change from baseline was -29.7 mg/dL in the overall population (P<0.001).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: adjusted mean difference versus placebo in change from baseline

atoms.canonical_statement: The adjusted treatment difference in HbA1c change from baseline was -0.23 percentage points in the overall population (P=0.024).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: adjusted mean difference versus placebo in change from baseline

atoms.canonical_statement: The adjusted treatment difference in high blood glucose index change from baseline was -3.4 in the overall population (P=0.005).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: adjusted mean difference versus placebo in change from baseline

atoms.canonical_statement: The adjusted treatment difference in time spent at 70–140 mg/dL was +14.4 percentage points in the overall population (P<0.001).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: adjusted mean difference versus placebo in change from baseline, percentage points

atoms.canonical_statement: The adjusted treatment difference in fructosamine change from baseline was -10.8 mg/dL in the overall population (P=0.019).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: adjusted mean difference versus placebo in change from baseline

atoms.canonical_statement: The between-group difference in change in 24-hour MAGE was -15.3 mg/dL in the overall population (P=0.010).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: difference versus placebo in change from baseline

atoms.canonical_statement: The between-group difference in change in 24-hour “distance traveled” was -37.5 mg/dL in the overall population (P=0.312).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: difference versus placebo in change from baseline

atoms.canonical_statement: The between-group difference in change in the standard deviation of 24-hour glucose was -4.7 mg/dL in the overall population (P=0.037).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: difference versus placebo in change from baseline

atoms.canonical_statement: Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 18/50 (36%) dapagliflozin participants and 10/50 (20%) placebo participants during the 4-week study.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: dapagliflozin incidence percent

atoms.canonical_statement: Urinary tract infection occurred in 3/50 (6%) participants in each treatment arm.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: dapagliflozin incidence percent

atoms.canonical_statement: Six insulin-stratum participants—3/27 assigned dapagliflozin and 3/25 assigned placebo—had documented symptomatic or probable symptomatic hypoglycemia; all such events were nonsevere.

concept.text: Documented symptomatic or probable symptomatic hypoglycemia

quantitative_result.effect_measure: dapagliflozin event count

atoms.canonical_statement: One dapagliflozin participant had a severe treatment-emergent adverse event of elevated blood creatinine and decreased glomerular filtration rate; it did not lead to treatment discontinuation.

concept.text: Severe elevated blood creatinine and decreased GFR

quantitative_result.effect_measure: dapagliflozin event count

atoms.canonical_statement: Adverse events led to study-drug discontinuation in 2/50 (4%) dapagliflozin participants and 0/50 placebo participants.

concept.text: Adverse event leading to study-drug discontinuation

quantitative_result.effect_measure: dapagliflozin incidence percent

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that dapagliflozin improved CGM-assessed glycemic control and variability compared with placebo over 4 weeks.

The authors reported apparently more robust glycemic effects with dapagliflozin plus metformin than with dapagliflozin plus insulin, while explicitly noting that this could reflect study design, combination regimen, or differences in disease severity and required further investigation.

The trial was powered for treatment differences only in the overall population, not in the metformin or insulin strata; stratum-specific P values were nominal and should not be treated as confirmatory subgroup evidence.

Patients in the insulin stratum were older and had higher BMI, FPG, HbA1c, systolic blood pressure, and longer diabetes duration than the metformin stratum, limiting causal interpretation of between-stratum differences.

The insulin stratum allowed rapid-acting mealtime insulin and had no run-in period to restabilize daily insulin doses after dapagliflozin initiation, so insulin-dose changes could have affected efficacy measurements.
No insulin diaries or detailed insulin dosing information were collected, preventing direct assessment of insulin-dose changes during the trial.
The treatment period lasted only 4 weeks, limiting assessment of durability and uncommon or longer-term safety outcomes.
The study evaluated glycemic and CGM surrogate outcomes rather than cardiovascular, renal, hospitalization, or mortality outcomes.
AstraZeneca supported the study and funded medical-writing and editorial assistance.

Several authors reported AstraZeneca relationships; S.B. Zhuplatov and Traci Mansfield were AstraZeneca employees and shareholders at the time of the research, Arie Katz was an AstraZeneca employee, and Poul Strange reported consulting for AstraZeneca.
